added.name: Section 1: Preface to the published revelations
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 1. Dated November 1, 1831, at Hiram, Ohio, in the context of a conference about publishing the revelations; Joseph Smith and assembled elders. The section is the preface to the published revelations: a worldwide proclamation, with Babylon and Idumea used as symbols. The apocalyptic Babylon is not mapped to an itinerary, and the Second Coming is not dated. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 2: Elijah and the hearts of the children
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 2. Dated September 21, 1823, at the Smith log home at Palmyra, New York, per the current heading; Joseph Smith and Moroni. The Elijah motif of turning the hearts of fathers and children is linked to later temple-key narratives. The section is an extract from a retrospective history, not a document written on the visitation date; no celestial coordinates are given. See also: “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 3: The lost manuscript pages
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 3. Dated July 1828 at Harmony, Pennsylvania; Joseph Smith and Martin Harris. It concerns the loss of 116 manuscript pages and the interrupted translation, and the text identifies several Book of Mormon peoples. No physical location is given for the missing manuscript, and no modern tribal ancestry is inferred from these names. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 4: A call to service for Joseph Smith Sr.
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 4. Dated February 1829 at Harmony. Joseph Smith Sr. receives instruction on service through his son, with qualifications for ministry. The harvest and the field are teaching metaphors, not farms or travel legs. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Joseph Smith Sr., Joseph Jr. and Hyrum”.

added.name: Section 5: Martin Harris asks for a witness
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 5. Dated March 1829 at Harmony. Martin Harris asks for a witness; the section speaks of three future witnesses, with conditional participation, and gives translation instructions. The prediction and conditional promise are not themselves the later witnessing event, and Jerusalem appears only as a comparison with the past. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”.

added.name: Section 6: Oliver Cowdery begins as scribe
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 6. Dated April 1829 at Harmony; the heading says the scribal work began on April 7. Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery: mutual support, the work of scribe and translator, and an inward spiritual witness. No route or surveyed location is added beyond the document’s setting. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Scribes and recorder”.

added.name: Section 7: John’s desired ministry
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 7. Dated April 1829 at Harmony. A revealed translation account in which the Lord speaks with John and then addresses Peter, explaining John’s desired ministry. The ancient narrated scene is not dated to April 1829, and no geographic itinerary is given for the translated John. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 8: Oliver Cowdery’s gifts
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 8. Dated April 1829 at Harmony. Oliver Cowdery’s gifts and his request to translate; revelation is described as communication to the mind and heart. The reference to Moses and the Red Sea is an explanatory comparison, not a nineteenth-century journey. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 9: Cowdery directed to continue writing
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 9. Dated April 1829 at Harmony. After an attempt to translate, Oliver Cowdery is directed to continue writing for Joseph Smith; the section describes a process of study and decision. No coordinates or exact date for the attempt are given beyond the month. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Scribes and recorder”.

added.name: Section 10: Response to the lost manuscript
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 10. Probably dated around April 1829 at Harmony, though portions may date to summer 1828. A response to the lost manuscript: the instruction to translate Nephi’s record through the account of Benjamin, a relationship between the texts produced. The whole section is not treated as one precisely dated revelation, and the alleged alterers of the manuscript are not identified without evidence. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 11: Hyrum Smith told to prepare
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 11. Dated May 1829 at Harmony, after the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood as the heading suggests. Hyrum Smith, Joseph’s brother, is told to study and assist the translation before preaching publicly. A call to prepare is not proof that he had already left on a mission. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Joseph Smith Sr., Joseph Jr. and Hyrum”.

added.name: Section 12: Joseph Knight Sr.
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 12. Dated May 1829 at Harmony. Joseph Knight Sr. gives material help to Joseph Smith and his scribe (heading); instructions on service and charity. The vineyard imagery does not identify a property. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 13: The words of the Aaronic ordination
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 13. Dated May 15, 1829, near Harmony. The reported ordination of Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery by John the Baptist, shown at the existing Harmony / Priesthood Restoration Site. No exact point in the forest is added, and the section does not date the visitation of Peter, James and John.

added.name: Section 14: David Whitmer called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 14. Dated June 1829 at Fayette, in the Whitmer household: the household of Peter Whitmer Sr. hosts the translation. David Whitmer is promised a witness and a ministry; the heading notes he later became one of the Three Witnesses. Zion here is a religious cause, not an established Missouri site in June 1829. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”.

added.name: Section 15: John Whitmer called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 15. Dated June 1829 at Fayette. John Whitmer is called to a ministry of repentance; the heading notes he later became one of the Eight Witnesses. That section 16 uses the same wording does not merge John with Peter Whitmer Jr., and no separate travel route is given. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”.

added.name: Section 16: Peter Whitmer Jr. called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 16. Dated June 1829 at Fayette. Peter Whitmer Jr. receives instruction for ministry; the heading notes he later became one of the Eight Witnesses. He stays a separate recipient from section 15, and no map feature is added. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”.

added.name: Section 17: Before the witnesses view the plates
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 17. Dated June 1829 at Fayette, before the witnesses viewed the plates. Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer and Martin Harris are told of a conditional witnessing of the plates and other objects; the text links them to Laban, the brother of Jared and Lehi. This is not a catalogue of recovered artifacts or independent evidence of ancient origin. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”, “Prospective witnesses of the plates”.

added.name: Section 18: The Twelve envisioned
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 18. Dated June 1829 at Fayette. Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery and David Whitmer: a future Twelve is envisioned, with Cowdery and Whitmer to seek them out, and the worth of souls is taught. The actual organization of the Twelve is not dated to 1829; the later fulfillment is kept distinct. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 19: Martin Harris and the cost of printing
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 19. Probably dated summer 1829 at Manchester. Martin Harris is told to finance the printing with his property; the section speaks of repentance and Christ’s suffering, in the context of the book’s publication. The older March 1830 dating is not kept as certain, and the passage on suffering is theological testimony, not a nineteenth-century occurrence. See also: “The Book of Mormon in the revelations”.

added.name: Section 20: The Articles and Covenants
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 20. Composed over 1829–1830 at or near Fayette, and probably recorded after April 6, 1830. Joseph Smith is named first elder and Oliver Cowdery second; the section sets out church organization, officers, baptism, the sacrament and membership. April 6, 1830 is not used as a secure birth date for Jesus or as the date of every part of the text. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 21: The church organized
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 21. Dated April 6, 1830, at the Peter Whitmer Sr. home in Fayette, at the organization meeting. Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery are sustained and ordain each other; instructions on records and leadership. The six founding participants are not necessarily everyone who attended. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 22: Baptism and authority
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 22. Dated April 16, 1830, at Manchester, amid a controversy over baptism and authority; instruction on the new covenant. No journey is added, and the section is a doctrinal description rather than a historical claim that all earlier Christian baptism was invalid. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 23: Five revelations at Manchester
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 23. Dated April 1830 at Manchester. Five revelations to Oliver Cowdery, Hyrum Smith, Samuel H. Smith, Joseph Smith Sr. and Joseph Knight, each with a different ministry responsibility. The five recipients are not collapsed into one missionary event. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Joseph Smith Sr., Joseph Jr. and Hyrum”.

added.name: Section 24: Duties of Smith and Cowdery
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 24. Dated July 1830 at Harmony. The duties of Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, with ministry directed at Colesville, Fayette and Manchester. The commanded circuit is not a proven completed itinerary. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 25: Emma Smith’s assignments
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 25. Dated July 1830 at Harmony. Emma Smith, Joseph’s wife, is to act as scribe, expound scripture and select hymns: a religious relationship and a record of women’s participation. She is not merely an entry as a supporting wife; her named assignments are kept. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Joseph Smith and Emma: spouses”.

added.name: Section 26: Common consent
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 26. Dated July 1830 at Harmony. Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery and John Whitmer: ministry at Colesville, farming, the next conference to the west, and common consent. No conference venue is inferred from the westward direction alone. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 27: The sacrament and a future gathering
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 27. Dated August 1830, with a second stage in September, at Harmony; the heading describes the two-stage writing. The emblems of the sacrament, an anticipated gathering with Moroni and other sacred figures, and a genealogy of priesthood keys. The future sacramental assembly is not an 1830 travel event, and the text’s writing history is kept apart from the experience it reports. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Priesthood genealogies”.

added.name: Section 28: Competing revelation claims
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 28. Dated September 1830 at Fayette. Oliver Cowdery, Hiram Page and Joseph Smith: competing claims to revelation; a proposed mission among those the text calls Lamanites; a future Zion near their borders. The attribution of deception is the text’s judgment, and no surveyed Zion site exists yet. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 29: Gathering, Millennium and resurrection
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 29. Dated September 1830 at Fayette, before the conference of September 26; six elders present. Gathering, the Millennium, resurrection, agency and the Fall, and the redemption of children. The apocalyptic sequence is not given calendar years or drawn as disaster areas. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 30: Three Whitmers called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 30. Dated September 1830 at Fayette after the conference; three revelations combined in 1835. David, Peter Jr. and John Whitmer: Peter is to go with Oliver Cowdery, and David is at his father’s house. John is directed to Philip Burroughs’ and the surrounding region (verse 10). Religious use of “brother” is not proof of biological kinship, and the 1835 editorial combination is not the date of the missionary departure. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 31: Thomas B. Marsh called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 31. Dated September 1830, following the conference; the heading does not specify the venue. Thomas B. Marsh is called to preach, with his family obligations and the prospect of their unity. The promise about his family is not evidence that each family member later converted. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 32: Pratt and Peterson join the western mission
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 32. Dated early October 1830 at Manchester. Parley P. Pratt and Ziba Peterson join Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. on the mission to the people the text calls Lamanites. The proposed mission’s western endpoints are unresolved. The historical term is kept with attribution and is not a genetic identification of all Indigenous peoples. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 33: Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 33. Dated October 1830 at Fayette. Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet are called to proclaim the gospel, with gathering and preparation. Nephi’s departure from Jerusalem is a scriptural comparison (verse 8), not their route; the vineyard and the eleventh hour are metaphors, not sites or clock times. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 34: Orson Pratt called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 34. Dated November 4, 1830, at the Whitmer home in Fayette. Orson Pratt, younger brother of Parley, is called to baptism, preaching and prophecy. The heading dates his conversion relative to the revelation; no exact baptism day is inferred here. See also: “Calls to preach”, “The Pratt and Cowdery brothers”.

added.name: Section 35: Sidney Rigdon as scribe
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 35. Dated December 7, 1830, at or near Fayette. Sidney Rigdon takes the scribal role in the Bible revision; he and Edward Partridge have arrived from Ohio; Oliver Cowdery and John Whitmer were earlier scribes. The “translation” of the Bible here is Joseph Smith’s revision project, not the discovery of an ancient manuscript. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Scribes and recorder”.

added.name: Section 36: Edward Partridge called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 36. Dated December 9, 1830, near Fayette. Edward Partridge is called and Sidney Rigdon lays hands on him; instruction on priesthood and mission. No travel path is added, and the wording of ordination or confirmation follows the text rather than an inferred office. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 37: Translation paused; Ohio ahead
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 37. Dated December 1830 near Fayette. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to pause the translation, strengthen the church at Colesville and then gather in Ohio, timed by Oliver Cowdery’s return. The directive documents an intended migration, not a completed arrival. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 38: The Fayette conference of January 1831
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 38. Dated January 2, 1831, at a conference in Fayette. Gathering in Ohio, care for the poor, a promised endowment of power, unity and a future land of inheritance, with a reference to Enoch’s Zion. The promised land is not mapped from this section alone, and the future wars are not given a computed year. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 39: James Covel instructed
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 39. Dated January 5, 1831, at Fayette. James Covel, a long-serving Methodist minister according to the current heading, is told to accept baptism and preach. Ohio is the commanded destination, explicitly not the eastern countries (verse 14). The older identification as Covill, a Baptist, is not repeated without documentary explanation. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 40: Covel’s rejection explained
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 40. Dated January 6, 1831, at Fayette. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon receive an account explaining why James Covel rejected the instruction. This is the text’s attributed explanation of motives, not independent psychological evidence. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 41: Partridge named first bishop
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 41. Dated February 4, 1831, at Kirtland. Joseph Smith has arrived from New York; Leman Copley offers land at Thompson; Edward Partridge is named the first bishop; housing and support for the translation. Kirtland and Thompson are kept distinct, and the appointment is not a later organizational chart of bishoprics. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Bishops and the bishop’s agent”.

added.name: Section 42: The law of the church
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 42. Dated February 9 and 23, 1831, at Kirtland: verses 1–72 and 73–93 belong to the two different dates. Church law: missionaries in pairs, consecration and property, care for the sick, discipline, and a promise of information about the New Jerusalem. Civil and criminal cases, and private and public reconciliation, are distinguished (74–93). No New Jerusalem location is inferred here. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 43: Who receives revelation for the church
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 43. Dated February 1831 at Kirtland. The authority to receive revelation for the church, disputed claims to it, the elders’ proclamation and teaching about the Millennium. No historical date is given for the Millennium, and no map of natural disasters is drawn. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 44: A conference summoned
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 44. Dated late February 1831 at Kirtland. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are told to summon a conference; legal organization and relief for the poor. The instruction and the June meeting are separate entries in the chronology. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 45: The Mount of Olives discourse
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 45. Dated March 7, 1831, at Kirtland. The discourse on the Mount of Olives and a future appearance; Enoch; the revision of the New Testament; gathering and the New Jerusalem as a refuge. The past discourse, the future prophecy and the 1831 writing are kept apart, and no predicted event is dated. See also: “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 46: Meetings and spiritual gifts
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 46. Dated March 8, 1831, at Kirtland. Access to meetings for those seeking truth, spiritual gifts and discernment. A reference entry, not a geographic journey. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 47: John Whitmer as historian
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 47. Dated March 8, 1831, at Kirtland. John Whitmer replaces Oliver Cowdery as historian and recorder, continuing the documentary record. No route is added, and the mandate to keep records is kept distinct from the records that actually survive. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Scribes and recorder”.

added.name: Section 48: Migration into Ohio
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 48. Dated March 10, 1831, at Kirtland. Migration from the East into Ohio; sharing and buying land, and a future city. An instruction to buy is not evidence that a named parcel was bought. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 49: The mission to the Shakers
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 49. Dated May 7, 1831, at Kirtland; the heading places the Shaker community near Cleveland, and its exact site is unresolved. Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, Leman Copley and the Shakers: marriage, baptism, diet and a disagreement about the Second Coming. The section’s polemical description is not a complete independent history of the Shakers. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 50: Discerning spiritual manifestations
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 50. Dated May 9, 1831, at Kirtland. Spiritual manifestations are evaluated; preacher and hearer understand each other and are edified. Joseph Wakefield and Parley P. Pratt are to strengthen the churches, John Corrill is also called, and Edward Partridge is rebuked (37–39). Spiritual discernment is not mapped as a scientific classification of physical things. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 51: Stewardships at Thompson
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 51. Dated May 20, 1831, at Thompson. Edward Partridge organizes properties, stewardships and a storehouse; Ohio is a temporary gathering place. Stewardships are not plotted without deeds, and Ohio is not implied to be a permanent endpoint. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bishops and the bishop’s agent”.

added.name: Section 52: Companions sent to Missouri
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 52. Dated June 6, 1831, at a conference in Kirtland, directing a gathering in Missouri. Pairs: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon; Lyman Wight and John Corrill; John Murdock and Hyrum Smith, by way of Detroit; Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre; Isaac Morley and Ezra Booth; Edward Partridge and Martin Harris to join Smith; David Whitmer and Harvey Whitlock; the Pratt brothers; Solomon Hancock and Simeon Carter; Edson Fuller and Jacob Scott; Levi Hancock and Zebedee Coltrin; Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith; Wheeler Baldwin and William Carter; Newel Knight and Selah J. Griffin. Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey are assigned east; Heman Basset is replaced by Simonds Ryder; Jared Carter and George James are ordained priests. The pairs and destinations are instructions, not completed itineraries, and section 56 revises the pairings. See also: “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Mission companions in section 52”.

added.name: Section 53: Sidney Gilbert as the bishop’s agent
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 53. Dated June 8, 1831, at Kirtland. Algernon Sidney Gilbert is made an elder and the bishop’s agent, for temporal administration, and is to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. He is not to be confused with Sidney Rigdon. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Calls to preach”, “Bishops and the bishop’s agent”.

added.name: Section 54: The Colesville migrants go on
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 54. Dated June 10, 1831, at Kirtland, addressed to the community at Thompson. Newel Knight leads the Colesville migrants after the agreement for Leman Copley’s farm breaks down, and they leave for Missouri. This records a failed settlement arrangement, not an assumed permanent inheritance at Thompson. See also: “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 55: William W. Phelps, printer
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 55. Dated June 14, 1831, at Kirtland. William W. Phelps, a printer: education and publication work and an assignment to Missouri. Phelps and Joseph Coe join Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon’s journey. The instruction to write schoolbooks does not identify a particular published edition. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 56: Companions revised
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 56. Dated June 15, 1831, at Kirtland. Thomas B. Marsh is now paired with Selah J. Griffin; Newel Knight remains to lead the Thompson group; Ezra Thayre’s assignment depends on his repentance. Obligations of the rich and the poor follow. The revoked instructions are superseded, not shown alongside as completed travel. See also: “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Revised companion assignments”.

added.name: Section 57: Independence named as Zion’s center
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 57. Dated July 20, 1831, in Jackson County, Missouri. Independence is identified as the center place of Zion and the place for a temple, which is distinct from the town; Sidney Gilbert’s store, William W. Phelps’s printing and Oliver Cowdery’s editing. The religious designation is not proof that the anticipated temple was built or that the whole county was bought. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Meanings of Zion”, “Bishops and the bishop’s agent”.

added.name: Section 58: Gathering administration in Zion
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 58. Dated August 1, 1831, in Jackson County, as the Colesville company arrives. Agency, repentance, the purchase of land and the administration of the gathering. Sidney Rigdon is to describe and dedicate the land and the temple spot; Joseph Smith, Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery are to return; Ziba Peterson’s office is removed pending his repentance. The promises and instructions to buy are not a completed land survey. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 59: Polly Knight and the Sabbath
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 59. Dated August 7, 1831, in Jackson County. Polly Knight, wife of Joseph Knight Sr., has died (the date is from the heading); the dedication of the land and temple spot precedes the revelation; the Sabbath and fasting. No burial location or historic site boundary is inferred. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “The Knight and Murdock couples”.

added.name: Section 60: Directions for the return east
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 60. Dated August 8, 1831, at Independence. The returning elders are directed to St. Louis; Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery are to go on to Cincinnati; the others preach on their way home in pairs. Edward Partridge supplies travel money, to be repaid as they are able. Permission for transport is not a confirmed route. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 61: On the Missouri River at McIlwaine’s Bend
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 61. Dated August 12, 1831, at McIlwaine’s Bend on the Missouri River. Joseph Smith and ten elders are returning by canoe toward Kirtland; William W. Phelps reports a vision; the travel is reorganized. Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery are directed toward Cincinnati, avoiding the water except by canal; Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith must stay together. The vision is not generalized into a scientific claim about hazards, and no modern location is invented for the changed river bend. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 62: Meeting at Chariton
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 62. Dated August 13, 1831, on the Missouri River at Chariton. The returning Smith party meets elders traveling toward Zion; discretion about transport and preaching. The parties moving in opposite directions remain distinct, with no single merged route. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 63: Back in Kirtland
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 63. Dated August 30, 1831, at Kirtland; the heading gives the return as August 27. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery have returned: purchases in Zion, warning and faith, the resurrection. Titus Billings is to dispose of his farm to travel to Zion the next spring; Newel K. Whitney is to keep his store and act as agent; Rigdon is to rewrite his rejected description of the land; Smith and Rigdon are to find homes. The Mount of Transfiguration, mentioned in passing, is not located, and the prophesied wars are not dated. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 64: Forgiveness, debt and the five-year hold
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 64. Dated September 11, 1831, at Kirtland. A move to Hiram for the Bible revision is planned, and a company is preparing to leave for Missouri in October; forgiveness and debt. Isaac Morley’s farm is to be sold but Frederick G. Williams’s farm kept; Kirtland is to be held for five years; the store of Newel K. Whitney and Sidney Gilbert is kept until the remaining disciples leave. The planned departures are not asserted as completed here, and “tithing” is not automatically the modern ten percent. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 65: A prayer and Daniel’s stone
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 65. Dated October 30, 1831, at Hiram. A prayer for the kingdom of the gospel and a millennial union, with the motif of Daniel’s stone. The mountain and the rolling stone are not a route on the ground or a dated conquest of the world. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 66: William E. McLellin’s mission
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 66. Dated October 29, 1831, at Hiram; section 66 precedes 65, so the order of sections does not give the date. William E. McLellin receives direction for a mission; the heading mentions his secret questions, which are not given here. He is to go east with Samuel H. Smith, not yet to Zion, and not to return until sent. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Revised companion assignments”.

added.name: Section 67: The Book of Commandments conference
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 67. Dated early November 1831 at Hiram. A conference on publishing the Book of Commandments and a controversy over the language of the revelations; the heading mentions the press at Independence. The proposed print run is not the number of copies actually produced or surviving. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 68: Missionary words, bishops and parents
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 68. Dated November 1, 1831, at Hiram, and expanded for the 1835 edition. Orson Hyde, Luke S. Johnson, Lyman E. Johnson and William E. McLellin: missionary words, bishops, and parents’ duty to teach. Oliver Cowdery is to carry the sayings to Zion; baptism at age eight. Not all the current wording is dated to 1831, and the claim of biological Aaronic descent remains doctrine. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Calls to preach”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 69: Manuscripts carried to Independence
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 69. Dated November 11, 1831, at Hiram. Oliver Cowdery carries manuscripts and funds to Independence; John Whitmer goes with him and gathers historical records. A travel mandate, not a day-by-day route; it links the roles of publisher and recorder. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Calls to preach”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 70: Stewards of the revelations
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 70. Dated November 12, 1831, at Hiram. Stewards of publication are appointed; spiritual labor and temporal equality. Stewardship is not merged with ownership of every manuscript. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

before.name: John, Peter and James in the revelations
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 7:1–8 records a dialogue between John the Beloved and Peter; 27:12 and 128:20 name Peter, James and John as messengers in the restoration narrative. This John is the apostle, not John the Baptist and not John Whitmer.

after.name: John, Peter and James in the revelations
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 7:1–8 depicts the Lord speaking with John the Beloved and then addressing Peter about their desires and ministry; 27:12 and 128:20 name Peter, James and John as messengers in the restoration narrative. This John is the apostle, not John the Baptist and not John Whitmer.

before.name: From Abel to Noah in the revelations
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Sections 84:16, 107:40–57, 124:75 and 138:40–41 name Abel, Cain, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah in lineage, ordination and vision contexts. Section 107 distinguishes ordination from parenthood. Section 84:16 says Abel was slain by his brother, who is not named there. The ordination ages are claims of the text; Enoch’s 430 years in section 107 and the 365 years of Genesis 5 are both kept (see “Priesthood genealogies”).

before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — The 1833 text gives dietary counsel and promised blessings and introduces itself as not given by commandment or constraint.
